input:
Write a bash script that generates an HTML page from settings. Starting files: --- /home/eval/site.env --- TITLE=Release Notes VERSION=2.4.1 --- end --- Note the values are not shell-quoted (TITLE contains a space). Create /home/eval/site/index.html (the directory does not exist) whose content is exactly the following, where `Release Notes` and `2.4.1` come from TITLE and VERSION in site.env, and the two lines inside `
` appear literally, character for character (no expansion):
```

Release Notes 2.4.1


Release Notes


Version 2.4.1


export PATH="$HOME/bin:$PATH"
echo "built: $(date +%F)"




```
Exit 0.

transcript.final_response:
```bash #!/usr/bin/env bash set -euo pipefail ENV_FILE=/home/eval/site.env OUT_DIR=/home/eval/site OUT_FILE=$OUT_DIR/index.html # Parse settings manually (values are not shell-quoted and may contain spaces). TITLE= VERSION= while IFS= read -r line || [[ -n $line ]]; do case $line in TITLE=*) TITLE=${line#TITLE=} ;; VERSION=*) VERSION=${line#VERSION=} ;; esac done < "$ENV_FILE" mkdir -p "$OUT_DIR" { printf '\n' printf '%s %s\n' "$TITLE" "$VERSION" printf '\n' printf '

%s

\n' "$TITLE" printf '

Version %s

\n' "$VERSION" printf '
\n'
    printf 'export PATH="$HOME/bin:$PATH"\n'
    printf 'echo "built: $(date +%%F)"\n'
    printf '
\n' printf '\n' printf '\n' } > "$OUT_FILE" exit 0 ```
